papers.title_en: Entropy-Regularized Probabilistic Gates for Sparse Model Discovery in Scarce-Data Federated Learning
papers.authors: Krishna Harsha Kovelakuntla Huthasana, Alireza Olama, Andreas Lundell
papers.evidence: 联邦学习中基于熵正则化概率门的稀疏模型发现
papers.tldr: 联邦学习在数据异构下训练稀疏模型对小样本高维场景易过拟合，且缺乏对参数空间不确定性的探索。本文研究熵正则化的概率门以维持不确定性，防止过早锁定稀疏结构，增强探索。在合成和真实数据上，该方法测试性能和稀疏恢复精度均优于Fed-IHT与剪枝FedAvg。为稀缺数据下联邦稀疏模型发现提供了新视角，强调保持训练不确定性的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning (ML) paradigm with collaboration among multiple clients without sharing data. FL is challenging under data heterogeneity and partial client participation. Learning sparse models is useful for communication and computational efficiency in FL, but it is especially difficult in the small-sample high-dimensional regime (d >> N) where optimization can yield parameter configurations that fail to generalize to unseen test data. While magnitude-based pruning doesn't account for uncertainty exploration in the parameter space, a formulation with probabilistic gates and an L0 constraint allows sampling from competing sparse configurations during training. In this work, we study entropy regularization of gate distributions as a mechanism to maintain uncertainty in sparse federated optimization by preventing early commitment to sparse support. We examine its impact under data heterogeneity, client participation heterogeneity, and sparsity. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show consistent improvements over federated iterative hard thresholding (Fed-IHT) and pruning after dense federated averaging (FedAvg) training, both in statistical performance on test data and in sparsity recovery accuracy.

papers.title_en: Towards Value-Constrained Credit Assignment in Fully Delegated AI Cooperatives
papers.authors: Young Yoon, Jimin Kim, Soyeon Park
papers.evidence: 去中心化遍历学习中的价值条件梯度过滤用于AI合作体
papers.tldr: 在完全委托AI合作社中，参与者以代理形式贡献数据并参与模型更新，但每个委托人对更新持有异质价值约束，传统分配机制无法区分有价值贡献。为此，本文提出基于遍历学习的价值约束信用分配框架，利用去中心化反向传播保留完整梯度路径，执行价值条件过滤，只对符合委托人偏好的更新分配信用。通过在线边际贡献信号和累积结算，实现细粒度归因。该方法避免了联邦平均的聚合质量损失，提供了更精确的贡献评估，为多元价值对齐的协作学习开辟新路径。
papers.abstract_en: We propose a framework for reward allocation in fully delegated AI cooperatives where humans are represented by agents that contribute data and participate in model updates under heterogeneous value constraints. The key idea is to credit only those updates that remain admissible after screening them against each principal's value profile. We formulate value-conditioned gradient filtering, online marginal contribution signals, and cumulative revenue settlement within a traversal learning (TL) substrate. TL is especially attractive here because it performs decentralized backpropagation without the quality loss associated with aggregation-centric distributed learning and, we argue, offers a finer attribution substrate than FedAvg-style federated learning by preserving explicit traversal and gradient paths. The framework is positioned against data valuation, federated contribution estimation, personalized federated learning, and pluralistic alignment.
